questions.q: Homoleptic octahedral complexes of a metal ion $′M^{3 +}′$ with three monodentate ligands ${L}_{1}, {L}_{2}and{L}_{3}$ absorb wavelengths in the region of green, blue and red respectively. The increasing order of the ligand strength is:
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
Observed order of wavelengths,& ${\lambda}_{abs}= {L}_{3} > {L}_{1} > {L}_{2}$.

(Red light has highest wavelength of 700 nm while blue is the shortest with a wavelength of about 480 nm)

So,~${∆}_{0}$ (strength of ligands) order~ will be ${L}_{2} > {L}_{1} > {L}_{3}$.

(As ${∆}_{0}\alpha\dfrac{1}{{\lambda}_{abs}}$ )

Hence, order will be ${L}_{2} > {L}_{1} > {L}_{3}$.

Therefore, Strength of ligand $∝ {∆}_{Absorption}$.

questions.q: The IUPAC name of ${K}_{3} [ Co ( {C}_{2}{O}_{4}{)}_{3} ]$ is:
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
Ligands that include a numerical prefix in the name use the prefixes bis for $2$, tris for $3$, or tetrakis for $4$ to indicate their number.

If the complex ion is an anion, we drop the ending of the metal name and add −ate.

In the given coordination compound, $Co$ is the cobalt metal,~${C}_{2}{O}_{4}^{2 -}$~are the ligands named as oxalato.

The charge on~$[ Co ( {C}_{2}{O}_{4}{)}_{3} ]$~is $- 3$ and oxalate is having~charge of $- 2$.

$X + 3 ( - 2 ) = - 3X = + 3$

Hence, the IUPAC~name of the compound~${K}_{3} [ Co ( {C}_{2}{O}_{4}{)}_{3} ]$~is Potassium trioxalatocobaltate$( III )$.

questions.q: Low oxidation state of metals in their complexes are common when ligands
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
When metal has low oxidation state, it has more electron density in d orbital. So it has more tendency to back donate electrons. Thus compound must have good& $\pi$ acceptor ligand.

~π backbonding, also called π backdonation, is when electrons move from an atomic orbital on one atom to an appropriate symmetry antibonding orbital on a π-acceptor ligand.It is especially common in the organometallic chemistry of transition metals with multi-atomic ligands such as carbon monoxide, ethylene or the nitrosonium cation. Electrons from the metal are used to bond to the ligand, in the process relieving the metal of excess negative charge. Compounds where π backbonding occurs include $Ni ( CO{)}_{4}$ and Zeise's salt.

The metal to ligand bonding creates a synergic effect which strengthens the bond between ligand& and the metal

ligand names + metal name(oxidation state)

${K}_{2}{MnO}_{4}$

$2 + x – 8 = 0$

$⇒ x = + 6$

Oxidation state of $Mn = + 6$

IUPAC Name is:

Potassium tetraoxidomanganate \left(VI\right)$
